Noise from blasting can be decreased by use of properly placed selective explosives. Use of delays and proper weight charges can also reduce the sound levels of the blast. In addition, blasting must comply with Mining Enforcement Safety Administration (MESA) noise regulations. Workmen, being made aware of high noise levels in specified areas, must take precautions such as wearing ear plugs.
Technological advances during the life of the leases may provide improved noise - muffling equipment. The terrain locally is rolling, rugged in sandstone cliff areas and partially forested. Such topographic features act as a natural sound barrier, to help mitigate the impacts of noise from mining operations.
Topography
Mined areas will be regraded to approximate the original contour. Spoil piles will be regraded to slopes less than 1:5 (one unit vertically to five units horizontally, about 11.5 degrees) except on the final highwall, which will be reduced to a slope not greater than 1:3 (about 19.5 degrees). The recontouring plan includes construction of a properly graded drainage system. Erosion will be minimized by prompt revegetation. Recontouring will be kept current within two spoil piles of the active pit.
Soils
Prior to mining, topsoils are mapped and samples from representative profiles analyzed to identify chemical hazards. Soils which are unsuitable as a plant growth medium due to chemical limitations will not be saved.
